Subject: Re: Kickoff — Performance SLO qualification

Thanks for the call today, Marissa — helpful framing. Quick recap from our side and a couple clarifying Qs: 

- Target production SLOs: p95 latency < 250ms for 512-token streaming responses; sustained throughput target ~200 requests/sec at 4 concurrent workers per pod.
- Streaming: we need server-sent events (chunked tokens) so the UI can render partial answers; client-side cancelation within 200ms of user action is required.
- Reproducibility: we want a repeatable benchmark that we can run in our staging AWS account — will need an HF-compatible model artifact or container/AMI and a deterministic harness.

Attached is a CSV of example prompt types and traffic mix (edgefin_benchmark_questions.csv). Next steps from EdgeFin: share a prioritized prompt set and define acceptable variance vs baseline.

Can Redwood share the benchmark harness and a short doc describing measurement definitions (what counts towards p95, how you handle tail latencies during cold start, whether KV cache warmup is included)?

Sofia
Head of ML Platform, EdgeFin

--

Great notes, Sofia — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and what we'll provide this week: 

1) Benchmark harness: we'll send a packaged harness (redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.tar.gz) that can run in your AWS staging account and publish a deterministic runbook. It includes load clients, streaming test harness, and data collection scripts.

2) Measurement definitions (attached draft SLO doc):
   - p95/p99 measured on per-response end-to-end latency from request send to last-token-delivered.
   - Streaming latency is measured per-token for first-byte and last-token; for p95 SLO we'll use last-token latency unless otherwise requested.
   - Cold starts: excluded from steady-state SLOs; we'll provide a separate cold-start baseline and include warmup procedure in the runbook.
   - Concurrency behavior: we'll report per-worker throughput and aggregate system throughput; runner supports ramps up to 500 RPS.

3) Prompt sets & reproducibility: please confirm the CSV you sent contains de-identified prompts. We'll include a seeded RNG for deterministic sampling, and a manifest to pin model versions and tokenization configs.

- EdgeFin: confirm prompt set & mark top-3 priority prompt types (Sofia) — by Thu 6/18

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology — runbook + next steps

Thanks Tom — answering the questions inline and attaching the runbook: 

- Streaming SLO & batching: the 250ms p95 last-token target assumes Redwood's default continuous batching with a configured max latency of 30ms to wait for batch fills. For single-request-per-connection patterns (no client-side batching), we still expect to meet p95 250ms for typical 512-token outputs on our T4-equivalent serving profile, but tail behavior improves with our batching + KV caching. We'll include a mode to disable batching in the harness so you can validate single-request behavior.

- Pod sizing: for your throughput and concurrency profile (200 RPS, 4 concurrent workers per pod) we recommend 1 x A10G-equivalent GPU per 8 workers as a starting point — guidance and a simple cost/throughput table are in the runbook. We'll run a short capacity test during the pilot to tune.

- Reproducibility & manifests: the harness pins tokenizers, model hash, and seed; please run the harness in staging with the expectation that network egress and NTP are stable. We also provide a Docker image if you'd rather not use the AMI.

Next steps / timeline: 
- EdgeFin (Sofia): confirm prompt priorities and mark any prompts that are PII-sensitive — by EOD Thu 6/18.
- EdgeFin (Procurement): we'll follow up with a pilot SOW and required compliance checklist — Marissa to share draft 6/19.
- Redwood (Neha & David): perform smoke run against a small subset of the CSV (Neha) and share example p95/p99 charts + raw CSV of per-request latencies (David) — by Fri 6/19.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.tar.gz (runbook + harness), SLO-draft-EF-v1.pdf
